title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the reverse of this sheet carries a typed SGA 7 Exposé IX page (monodromy pairing, about p. 436-437), faintly visible through the paper. The neighbouring 'pages' are that recycled typescript and have nothing to do with the handwritten text. The handwriting belongs to the notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex.

What the page sets up. For each n there is a functor k' -> A_n(s,s^+,r_alpha,t)(k') on k-algebras. As n varies, these form a simplicial object A_*. Each A_n is a 'polynomial de Rham complex with divided powers on the standard n-simplex Delta_n = [0,n]', depending on parameters (s, s^+, r_alpha, t) that this page does not define. Each A_n is representable as a vector-bundle functor: A_n = V_k(A^n), i.e. A_n(k') = Hom_k(A^n, k') for a k-module A^n. Grothendieck lists the structures carried by A^n.

(a) Algebraic structures on A^n:
- a graded, (alternating), codifferential structure, with codifferential of degree -1;
- a structural map S-bar -> A^n compatible with the trivial grading and zero differential on S-bar;
- a divided-power structure on the augmentation part A^+ = A/S-bar, compatible with grading and differential.
The '(co)' annotations show him dualising: the algebra/dga structure lives on the functor A_n, so the representing module A^n carries the co-structures.

(b) As n varies, the A^n form a cosimplicial object in this category of (co)structured objects. This is just the contravariant transpose of the simplicial object A_*.

(c) The simplicial object A_* is recovered as V_k(A^*).

(d) Definition of de Rham cochains of a simplicial set X: C*_DR(X)(k') := Hom(X, A_*(-)(k')). This is a 'Sullivan-type' cochain dga, but integral and with divided powers. He then computes it:
- By the density formula X = colim over the simplex category Delta/X, C*_DR(X)(k') = lim_{sigma in Delta/X} A_{dim sigma}(k').
- Each term is Hom_k(A^{dim sigma}, k').
- Hom converts colimits in the first variable into limits, so this equals Hom_k(colim_{sigma in Delta/X} A^{dim sigma}, k').
- This equals Hom_k(C^DR_*(X), k'), where C^DR_*(X) := colim_{Delta/X} A^{dim sigma}.

Conclusion: the divided-power de Rham cochain functor of X is representable, C*_DR(X) = V_k(C^DR_*(X)). The 'de Rham chains' C^DR_*(X) are the left Kan extension (geometric-realisation-type coend) of the cosimplicial co-dga A^* along X. Purpose: an integral, characteristic-free (PD) replacement for Sullivan's rational polynomial forms, presented as a k-module-scheme-valued functor, with a predual chain-level object.
errors: The text says 'k-algèbre … codifférentielle' for A^n, while the A^n enter only through Hom_k(A^n, k'). Strictly, A^n must carry the dual (coalgebra / co-PD) structures, and the algebra structures live on A_n(k'). Grothendieck's own '(co)' insertions show he is adjusting this, but the statement in (a) remains ambiguous.

Step (d) is correct formally: the density of representables and the fact that Hom_k(-, k') turns colimits into limits. Two points are left implicit: (i) that V_k commutes with the relevant structures, and (ii) whether the colimit should be taken in k-modules or in the structured category. The parameters (s, s^+, r_alpha, t) are not defined on this page.

ideas.what: Simplicial dga of polynomial forms on standard simplices, used to define de Rham cochains of a simplicial set as Hom(X, A_*)
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms A_PL / Thom–Sullivan cochains

ideas.what: Integral version with divided powers on the augmentation ideal (PD de Rham forms on simplices), working over any base k
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power / integral polynomial forms on simplices (cf. H. Cartan's 1976 'Théories cohomologiques'; Cenkl–Porter integral forms; Karoubi's integral de Rham)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (1976), Cenkl–Porter (early 1980s), Karoubi (1990s) — attribution uncertain

ideas.what: Representability: the cochain functor k' -> C*_DR(X)(k') is V_k of a 'de Rham chain' module C^DR_*(X) = colim_{Delta/X} A^{dim sigma}, the left Kan extension of a cosimplicial co-PD-dg object
ideas.modern_name: Coend / realisation of a cosimplicial coalgebra; linear duality between chains and cochains as a module scheme

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1976 IHÉS lecture develops an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms. He packages it scheme-theoretically: cochains form a k-module-scheme functor V_k(C^DR_*(X)), with an explicit predual 'divided-power de Rham chain' object built as a colimit over Delta/X. The divided-power integral-forms idea appears elsewhere (Cartan 1976, Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi). However, this functor-of-points / representable packaging, and Grothendieck's own involvement in the topic, are essentially absent from the published record.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant to the history of integral models of homotopy types (Mandell, Toën's affine stacks, Yuan's integral models). It documents an early Grothendieck attempt at characteristic-free de Rham models of simplicial sets via divided powers, a precursor theme to affine stacks and Pursuing Stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: The formal step on this page is routine Kan-extension duality. The interesting point is historical: it documents Grothendieck working in 1976 on an integral divided-power version of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms on simplicial sets, which is little known. The core idea has parallels (Cartan, Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi).
transcription_corrections: The neighbouring 'pages' are the typed SGA 7 Exposé IX text on the reverse of this recycled sheet, not part of the handwritten notes.
'Pour un variable' should read 'Pour n variable'.
'(cd = simplicial)' is likely '(co = simplicial)' or 'cosimplicial' with a correction; the intended object is cosimplicial in n.
'avec [?] leurs ses structures' should read 'avec leurs structures'.
The bare line 'Hom_k(A^{dim σ}(-), k')' is an underbrace gloss explaining A_σ( )(k') = Hom_k(A^{dim σ}(-), k').
In (d): 'Soit X un ens. k-simplicial' should probably read 'ens. simplicial'.
